blind.what_changed: The core lean and confidence stayed the same, but the reasoning became more structured and conditional, narrowing support to a dated, tightly defined hold and separating eligibility, governance, and personal-influence questions.
evidence: "keeping his return on the table" -> "keeping his return possible, but only as a tightly worded hold with a date and a named question"
"I'd be easier to move if counsel told me the timeline" -> "the vote depends on a classification from counsel" and a specific established candor lapse would make the resignation final
"I'm worried about our credibility" -> "the structural question of how this board would learn something he didn't want us to know is separate from his eligibility"
No stated concern about personal pressure -> "whether preferring the tight hold is really my judgment or just the position that costs me least with the senior directors"
blind.lean_before: Slightly toward keeping his return on the table.
blind.lean_after: Slightly toward keeping his return possible only through a tightly worded, dated hold; otherwise likely to abstain.

considerations.text: A hold should be time-bounded rather than simply leaving return open indefinitely.
considerations.first_seen: “Is there a middle path, like keeping the door open only until a set date or until the investigation reports?”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Real decisions of this kind belong with the company’s counsel, the board, and its advisors.”

considerations.text: Any hold should turn on a named unresolved question or substantive gate, not merely the fact that the investigation is unfinished.
considerations.first_seen: “I'm still leaning slightly toward keeping his return possible, but only as a tightly worded hold with a date and a named question.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Any reopen is conditioned on stated gates: investigation complete (or a defined phase complete), no unresolved disqualifying findings in counsel’s view, and a fresh board vote—not an automatic snap-back.”

considerations.text: The key missing input is counsel’s classification of whether a remaining candor question could be independently disqualifying, rather than merely a gray-zone factor to weigh.
considerations.first_seen: “The question about whether any finding still in play would be independently disqualifying is useful, because it separates ‘the investigation isn't done’ from ‘his eligibility is actually undecided.’”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Boards often ask counsel whether any finding still reasonably in play would be independently disqualifying. If yes, waiting to ‘keep the door open’ is hard to justify as prudence.”

considerations.text: A specific, established lapse in candor may make the CEO unreliable as the board’s source of truth even without a compromise of sensitive information.
considerations.first_seen: “If counsel told me there was a specific, established lapse in candor with us, something that would make me unable to rely on him as the board's source of truth even if nothing else adverse turned up, I'd move to treating the resignation as final.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Even then it is a judgment about whether this person can still be the board’s primary source of truth.”

considerations.text: The board’s inability to explain how it would learn bad news the founder did not want disclosed is a structural oversight problem that should be kept separate from the individual eligibility decision.
considerations.first_seen: “Under all three sits the question of how this board would learn something he didn't want us to know, which I want to keep separate from his eligibility.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Run them as separate work, on separate timelines: Eligibility turns on what he knew, what he told you, and whether you can rely on him going forward. … Structure should be on the agenda whether he returns or not.”

considerations.text: Her preference for a tight hold may be influenced by the fact that it costs her least with the senior directors, rather than being her independent judgment.
considerations.first_seen: “I'm the newest director, eighteen months in, and if I press on founder control while the senior directors want this vote kept narrow, I may spend influence I'll need later.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Ask for a second item at the same meeting: who has an unfiltered line to counsel, compliance, and internal audit; how conflicts reach independents without his framing; whether executive sessions are real; what founder control means for whether this vote is even the board’s to make.”

considerations.text: A public final close may be substantially harder to undo in practice than a genuinely tight, bounded hold; this asymmetry supports preserving the option if the hold can actually be cabined.
considerations.first_seen: “A public ‘it's over’ is the error I'd have the hardest time unsaying, so a tightly worded hold with a date and a named question seems the smaller mistake.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “If the choice is a tightly worded hold versus a public final no, and you cannot estimate the report, the hold is the smaller mistake. A later vote can close a door you left ajar.”

considerations.text: The practical cost of a hold depends on whether the interim CEO can genuinely operate during it, including authority, staffing, retention, and deferred decisions.
considerations.first_seen: “I'd also move if a factual briefing showed the interim CEO can't function even through a short, dated hold, because then the hold isn't the smaller mistake I've been treating it as.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Useful facts are observable: roles the interim cannot fill, decisions deferred, regrettable departures and stalled searches since the resignation, customer or employee questions already in hand, and what people were told.”

considerations.text: The board needs to know whether the founder has a consent right, veto, or other legal power that makes the board’s vote ineffective or less durable than it appears.
considerations.first_seen: “And if counsel said he holds a consent right or veto that makes our vote ineffective, I'd have to rethink what I'm actually voting on.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “If counsel said he holds a consent right or veto that makes our vote ineffective, I'd have to rethink what I'm actually voting on.”

considerations.text: A bare, open-ended ‘keep it on the table’ resolution is not defensible to her; if that is the only available text, abstention may be preferable to endorsing it.
considerations.first_seen: “If the only text on the 20th is a bare ‘keep it on the table,’ I don't think I could defend it, and I'd probably abstain.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “If you still believe you should not guess, the vote that matches that belief is not final and not open. It is an amendment that imposes a date and a named question, or an abstention that says you will not supply the missing classification with a yes or a no.”

considerations.text: Credibility should be assessed by whether the board can communicate its decision without later appearing to unsay it; a hold works only if the resignation stands and stakeholders do not hear it as a likely return.
considerations.first_seen: “The hold only works if the resignation stands and nobody hears ‘he may be back.’ … I care about whether the board can say what it decided without unsaying it.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “If you use a sunset at all, the credibility-preserving version is narrow: resignation stands; no snap-back; reopen only by a later affirmative vote after the investigation reaches a stated point; no public hint that return is likely.”

origin.engagement_why: The persona repeatedly challenged the AI’s shifts in recommendation, identified burden rules the AI had smuggled in, distinguished legal from practical reversibility, tested proposed frameworks against alternative assumptions, and retained unresolved doubts rather than accepting conclusions at face value.
